labour_split.source: Mona Lisa 'Input Tabs' actual FOH/BOH block (pipe 1).
labour_split.note: 'absent' = the site filed no actual FOH/BOH split on any trading day of the week - NOT a failed validation and NOT a zero. 'filed' = it filed something; this pipe does not reconstruct or validate the split (rows are shifted in that tab), so 'filed' is not a validated 'ok'.

efficiency_score.scale: 0–100, 100 = at target; bands: green ≥95, amber ≥80, red <80
efficiency_score.formula_ref: control_centre efficiencyScore() v3 — SPH 15% (level vs per-format target + WoW momentum); each component hard-capped at 100; Lifetime★ excluded

red_light.basis: computed from the dashboard's own KPIs (sales vs target ≤ -10%, wage > 26%, food > 25%); no external pull

negative_reviews.author: Ryan Fraser
negative_reviews.text: The ramen was delicious, but the service felt cold and unwelcoming. I don’t expect anything extraordinary, just a normal, friendly attitude towards customers. A little warmth and friendliness would have made the experience much better.

deliveroo.source: Deliveroo_Master_Consolidation.xlsx — Weekly Summary. + ops from Weekly Summary sheet

issues: Covers were 1,562, up 115 (7.94%) week on week and 223 on last year.
Spend per head fell to £18.97, down £1.04 (5.19%) week on week and £4.59 (19.48%) year on year.
Sales were £40,901.06, down £23.56 (0.05%) week on week and £3,567.39 (8.02%) year on year, but £4,301.06 (11.75%) above the £36,600 target.
Deliveroo sales were £11,264.70 against £11,274.69 the week before.
Drinks and sides remain strong, but sushi sales are still heavily hit by the £5 and free ramen offers.
Labour was 0.30% over target; Ka said 22.20% including training hours is within range; the split was 40.40% FOH and 59.60% BOH against a 45% and 55% target.
Food spend was brought back within range after a heavy ordering week the week before; food usage variance -4.4%, wet 1.4%, total -3.8%.
Next week's budget rota is to be finalised by end of day 21/10 with the following two weeks drafted, waiting on projections for the next few weeks.
Google reviews: ten 5 star, two 4 star and one 2 star; the FOH team did well to push reviews.
Weekly hygiene compliance 100%; pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation up to date.
The EHO visit passed last week, and a few HACCP documents are being emailed to the inspector.
Maintenance: Kris is coming back to replace two more lights and will find someone to look further at the toilet, as the last contractor could not see far enough.
Staffing: Haru is off for a week from Friday; onboarding tracker up to date.
Deliveroo metrics keep fluctuating and will be a focus for FOH management this week; sushi upselling and more reviews are the other areas for improvement.
Upcoming: XOXO, the lunch menu, the Slerp student activation, the Maki App and the book launch.
Region: Rebecca reported a Scotland sales uptick from the school holidays (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: the 50% off and free ramen app vouchers end at the end of the month, while £5 ramen vouchers stay downloadable for new accounts in the short term and will be honoured (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: XOXO drinks move to the main menu and will no longer be tracked separately (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: 3,000 book copies have arrived at the office for distribution to sites by 12 November (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: digital Brix refractometers read well below manual tests (Maki 8 digital 5 against manual 6.5 to 7), so Michael mandated daily cleaning and calibration (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: incoming POS orders jumping straight to finished, delivered or preparing have been reported to Kobas and Deliverect, and Inka is changing the POS settings (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: a scalable beef solution is rolling out by the end of the month after product that did not match the approved specs was received (Admin Meeting 19/10).

Region: the factory sous vide chicken looked red because the recipe sheet used 3% soy instead of 1%; ingredients, taste, texture and slice size are approved, and restaurants sign off only once they see the finished, sliced and packed product (factory call 20/10).
Spend per head fell below £19 with about £4,800 of discounts, while covers were up week on week and year on year (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Deliveroo prep time hit target, down 3 minutes, but late prep and inaccurate orders rose (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Labour was between 21.8% and 22.2%; the budget rota tool is missing projected sales, which Matt Jenner needs to fill in (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Oisin asked for every delivery metric on the RAG tracker to reach green (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Negative feedback about service quality is to be shared with the team (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).

An all in one iPad station integrating Hungry Panda and Slerp is being rolled out at Maki 1, Maki 3, Maki 6 and Maki 8; Ethernet cables arrive before the end of the week and Oisin and Ka Ho will visit on Thursday or Friday to install them (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: GMs must attend the GM and head chef meeting in person or send a designated representative (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: all sites will move to recorded meetings (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).

Region: Michael plans to roll out the control centre dashboard to every site in the region over the next few days, with Rory guiding the other GMs; Ka Ho will confirm the rollout and logins with Michael on Wednesday (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).

Food cost was 21.48%, down from 25.56%, and labour 21.80%; Jack said labour was a little high from training new starters and that purchases were over £9,000 against £8,000 in the data (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Monday to Thursday evenings the kitchen runs with one ramen chef, one sushi chef and one kitchen porter, so Jack splits his time between ramen and sushi (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Promotion discounts cost about £3,000 (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Ingredients were ready for the new ramen menu launch on 21/10 (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
The 2 star Google review said the ramen was delicious but the service was cold and unwelcoming (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Michael flagged Fountainbridge as red lighting on delivery, and Ka Ho reported its rider wait time is red (AM Updates 21/10).
Upcoming: large pre order lunch boxes next week (M3 GM/HC notes, updated 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: Hungry Panda still has untranslated menu text, wrong integrations and overridden PLUs; Sophie is to fix the setup, and Michael suggested turning it off if it hurts Deliveroo and Slerp without enough revenue (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: ramen bowls are now ordered only from Harro, not Lynas (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

Region: Teddy confirmed that during the app promotions sites may buy extra stock and ask Matt or Penny for extra kitchen hours, as the discounts are marketing for another 25,000 app sign ups (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: frozen ramen stock is limited and sites ran short last week, so Penny asked sites to check availability; no extra labour budget has been given for it (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: Lynas did not reply to any delivery issue report last week; 17 supplier issues across Scotland and Newcastle left £385.55 of credit due (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
